content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"The record cites ROI pages and ties the alcohol-policy reprimand to witness reports and the Agency's pretext analysis, but the path to the conclusion is incomplete, for example the Manager's alleged drinking was rejected as lacking 'preponderant evidence' without stating what was examined, and the 'no evidence' findings on incidents 1-4 and 6-11 are not traced to specific material."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Many characterizations are attributed (Complainant's affidavit, Witness 1 and 2, the Medical Provider, management officials, ROI page cites), but the alcohol-policy witnesses are unnamed ('Witnesses reported'), claims like 'no other officers engaged in similar behavior' rest on unspecified testimony, and the claim 5 finding on late reporting cites no source."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Key dates are given (Oct 24, 2020; Dec 3, 2020; May 5, 13, 14, 2021), but the SOT on May 13 is listed after the May 14 reprimand, the December 2020 meeting is undated beyond the month, and there are no dates for the EEO complaint, prior EEO activity, or the investigation and decision."},"rc4":{"status":"review","note":"The Chief issued the reprimand and the Agency applied a prima facie/pretext framework, but the record does not identify who made the SOT decision or the final decision, what discipline criteria or thresholds applied, or whether Witness 1/Witness 2 and the Manager's responses to the sexual-comment allegations were considered."},"rc5":{"status":"gap","note":"Because the evidence-to-conclusion links, source identification, chronology and decision-maker detail are each only partly documented, an independent reviewer could not assess from this summary alone whether the finding of no discrimination or harassment is supported, and would need the full ROI."}}}
